items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I played Milestones at the West End on March 11, 1974 with Paul Quinichette and Matthew Gee, and Sam Woodyard.

ctx.x: Oh they were huge Basie enthusiasts, but that doesn’t mean they weren’t huge Benny Goodman enthusiasts, huge Fletcher Henderson enthusiasts. I would say that — I would say they didn’t have a Basie preference to my knowledge. I would say that my befriending more Basie alumni than say the Ellington people — remember the Ellington people, some of them still were in the band and therefore were not full time residents of

New York City, much less residents of the Hollis area. I knew Russell Procope well but he was largely gone. I eventually became quite close to Sam Woodyard, but this was later. I mean then it was the Basieites, and then through me having these unusual extra- parental associations I would say that my parents became more Basie core because when I emerged professionally that’s my first idea was a group of these Basie alumni playing the early Basie repertoire, to give some context to these gigs, and to play…
For you what was it about the Basie sound that made it distinctive?
